relevance_note: Table 2 lists the ALDH5A1 genotype and zygosity for each of 58 numbered SSADHD patients ('Allelic variants, zygosity, resultant proteins combination, and eventual protein impairment effect of the SSADHD patients included in the study').
method_note: Read the whole Markdown (Research Square preprint text with a note that the version of record appeared in Human Genetics). Individual-level data exist only in Table 2 (58 patients; columns Patient, Allele_1, Allele_2, Zygosity, Protein variants combination, Effect). The Patient column holds bare index numbers, so labels are 'Table 2 #<n>'; the Results text refers to the same people as '#1', '#5', 'patient # 19' etc. A short Python script in the scratch directory transcribed Table 2 (both blocks) and the Table 1 nucleotide-to-protein mapping; I checked the output row by row against the tables. Consanguinity 'yes' only for rows whose zygosity carries the '*' footnote defined as '* Consanguinity.' (#21-25, #29, #32, #33, #45); unstarred rows are 'not reported', not 'no'. Homozygous patients have one variant row; compound heterozygotes two. Protein descriptions come from Table 1 (variant-level table) where it maps the exact printed cDNA string. Variant type is filled only where the text names the exact variant with a class (splice-site list, 'non-sense mutation (c.1234C > T)', missense statements for c.278G>T, c.1226G>A, c.803G>A, c.1005C>A; 6p22.3 deletion) or names the person (#1: 'two nonsense variants'); classes were not derived from HGVS. Pathogenicity left 'not reported': the only statements ('32 ALDH5A1 pathogenic variants', 'the 32 allelic variants ... were pathogenic') are about the cohort's variants in general (D-29). In silico predictions (SIFT/PolyPhen/CUPSAT/SpliceAI) are not functional assays and were not recorded as functional evidence. No individual-level sex, age, ethnicity or clinical features are given: all phenotype data are group counts in Table 4 / Results (e.g. '30 (52%) had ataxia'), which exclude no one and observe no one, so the checklist is 'not reported' for everyone and phenotypic_features is empty. Per-person severity statements (top CSS quartile, CSS >= 19.25: #1, #5, #11, #12, #16, #23, #35, #36, #37, #47, #51, #53, #54; lowest quartile, CSS < 15: #4, #14, #15, #18, #28, #29, #33, #34, #43, #44, #50, #56; '#19' milder clinical outcome) are composite severity scores, not checklist features, and were not recorded as features. Contradictions: (1) the text describes 'patient # 59' (c.1015-3C > G plus c.1234C > T, severe course with drug-resistant seizures) but Table 2 has only 58 patients; that genotype matches Table 2 #55, but I did not assign #59's facts to #55 and created no 59th person. (2) c.526G > A is G176R in Table 1 and in silico text but 'G176E' in Table 2 (#11, #36); protein left null for this variant. (3) c.517C > T is R173C in Table 1 but 'A173C substitution (c.517C > T)' in text; c.1558G > C is G520R in Table 1 but 'G520A substitution' in text; protein left null for both. (4) #37 Allele_1 printed 'c.278C > T' (elsewhere c.278G > T) and #44 printed 'c608C > T' (twice); recorded as printed, no protein or type attached. (5) The text says the 12 most severe patients had no individuals with multiple homo/heterotetramers and only catalysis impairment, but Table 2 gives #50 and #56 'Mixed protein population' and #50 'Stability/folding'; it also says all top-quartile patients had stability/folding/oligomerization defects while #37 is 'Catalysis**' and #1 'No protein'. (6) Table 1's first block is garbled by reference-list text (row for c.526G > A and following rows). (7) Protein spans for variants in Table 1's first block (c.612G > A, c.1234C > T, c.1597G > A, c.608C > T, c.803G > A, c.967_968dupCA, c.1226G > A, c.1323dupG) are about 372 characters, because the converted cells are padded with spaces; they are the shortest contiguous row segment from the cDNA cell to the protein cell.
